propositions: Signed gate verdicts currently record only a model string and cannot distinguish between first-class providers (Anthropic, Bedrock) and best-effort tier (custom base_url), preventing consumers from rejecting off-tier verdicts

A new additive `provider_provenance` object must be stamped into verdicts containing provider name, model, endpoint host (without credentials), tier classification, and effective capability record, without modifying the existing `model` field to preserve backward compatibility

The provenance record must be assembled once per run in `runner.py` from primitives already in scope, reusing the capability record computed at execution time rather than recomputing it, and must never be synthesized at verdict sites where no LLM actually ran

Credential material from `base_url` and `api_key` must never appear in the persisted sidecar payload; `urlparse(base_url).hostname` (not `.netloc`) correctly strips userinfo before persisting the endpoint host

The new `provider_provenance` key must be threaded through all three sidecar verdict assembly sites (plan_review, completion, code_review) and through gate recovery paths via the orchestrator's `finalize_verdict` function
Legacy sidecar payloads lacking the `provider_provenance` key must remain loadable and their signatures must still verify, validating the additive-only design
